summary: A. B. Gajendragadkar was an Indologist who served as a Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and as a Lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College, Dharwad.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, Muller earned his PhD at Stony Brook University (1988) and studied at the University of Virginia (~1989–1993). He was a professor at Toyo Gakuen University (~1997–2008) and the University of Tokyo (~2008–2019).

A. H. Armstrong studied at Jesus College (~1928–1932) and worked in philosophy. He held academic posts at Swansea University (~1936–1939), the University of Malta (~1939–1943), Cardiff University (~1947–1950), and the University of Liverpool (~1950–1972).

A scholar of linguistics and Indology, Ramanujan studied at the University of Mysore, Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1946–1950), and Indiana University (~1959–1963). He taught at Baroda College (~1958–1959), the University of Chicago (~1962–1993), and Harvard University (~1987–1988).
A. N. Krishna Aiyangar was an Indologist who served as Joint Editor of Brahmavidyā: The Adyar Library Bulletin at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1940–1942).
A. N. Narasimhia was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who completed his doctoral studies under Ralph Lilley Turner (attested 1941) and held a post at the University of Mysore.

Jackson was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies who studied at Columbia University (~1879–1886) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1887–1889). He served as a professor at Columbia University (~1886–1889, ~1895–1935).
A. W. Barber, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1984. He held a post at the University of Calgary (attested 1998).

Aaron P. Proffitt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who completed an MA at the University of Colorado Boulder and a PhD at the University of Michigan (~2009–2015). He was appointed assistant professor at University at Albany, SUNY (~2016).

Abdur Rehman, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham (attested 1988). He served as an assistant professor of archaeology at the University of Peshawar (attested 1988).

Abel Bergaigne was a French Indologist and linguist who studied under Michel Bréal (~1867–1869). He held posts as a répétiteur at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1888) and taught at the University of Paris (~1877–1888).

Abigail I. MacBain is a scholar in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who earned an MA from McMaster University (attested 2008), where she studied under faculty including Mark Rowe, James A. Benn, and Shayne Clarke.
Abraham Zablocki is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his PhD at Cornell University. He held an academic post at Agnes Scott College (attested 2008).

Achim Bayer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his MA under David P. Jackson and his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen (2005). He was a research associate at LMU Munich (2004–2006).

Adalbert Bezzenberger was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1869–1874) under Theodor Benfey and at LMU Munich (~1872–1873). He held a post at the University of Göttingen (~1874–1880).
Adalbert Kuhn, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp (~1833–1837). He later served as Direktor of the Köllnisches Gymnasium (~1870–1881).

Adam Bowles is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies under Greg Bailey (attested 2004). He served as a senior lecturer in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland (attested 2016–2018).
Adam Hardy is a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at The Royal Grammar School, High Wycombe, and held a post at Cardiff University (~2003).
Adam Pearcey is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier.

Adeu Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers including Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima, Samten Gyatso, and Chögon Rinpoche, and taught Tsoknyi Rinpoche.
